Sobriety

suh-BRY-uh-tee -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, BRY. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Sobriety is seriousness or clear-headedness.

She answered the reporters' questions with a sobriety that ended the joking at once.

Worked Example

The rest of the crew is still trading jokes when the pilot's voice comes over the radio -- level and unhurried, giving the fuel figure and the nearest airfield in the same steady tone she uses for the weather.

That steadiness is sobriety: seriousness joined to clear-headedness. Sobriety is not gloom -- it is the calm, unrattled gravity of someone who understands exactly how much a moment matters.

How Sobriety Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

seriousness

seriousness: a grave and earnest manner

solemnity

solemnity: dignified, weighty seriousness

levelheadedness

levelheadedness: calm good judgment under pressure

Antonyms

frivolity

frivolity: lack of seriousness

giddiness

giddiness: light-headed silliness

How Strong Is It? — seriousness → solemnity → sobriety

seriousness vs. sobriety

seriousness vs. sobriety: Seriousness is the plain word for the same manner; sobriety adds clear-headedness to it -- a serious person may still panic, while someone who meets a crisis with sobriety keeps their judgment intact.

solemnity vs. sobriety

solemnity vs. sobriety: Solemnity is heavier and more ceremonial: a memorial is conducted with solemnity, but a surgeon assesses a difficult case with sobriety -- grave, yes, but still working.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — so-

prefix — so-: without (Latin se-)

root — ebri-

root — ebri-: drunk (Latin ebrius)

suffix — -ety

suffix — -ety: state or quality of (Latin -itas)

Put it together

Put it together: Sobriety comes from Latin sobrius, usually explained as se- ('without') plus ebrius ('drunk'). English kept both branches: staying away from alcohol, and -- the sense taught here -- the clear, steady seriousness of a mind fully in command of itself.

Use the root in a new word: inebriated

Use the root in a new word: inebriated: The play's comic innkeeper staggers on stage pretending to be inebriated.

Root Check

Word Choice

Sobriety has two lives. In health and law it means abstaining from alcohol. In the sense taught here -- the one the ISEE tests -- it means seriousness and clear-headedness: 'she assessed the damage with sobriety,' 'a moment that called for sobriety.' Read the surrounding sentence to tell which sense is meant; if the passage is about manner and judgment rather than drinking, it is this one.
